title: Germany – Construction project management services – Projektsteuerungsleistungen - Einrichtung eines Technik-, Ausbildungs- und Logistikzentrums für die Feuerwehr Bergisch Gladbach
description: Die Infrastruktur- und Projektgesellschaft Bergisch Gladbach mbH (IPGL), eine 100% Tochtergesellschaft der Stadt, plant die Errichtung eines Technik-, Ausbildungs- und Logistikzentrums für die Feuerwehr Bergisch Gladbach auf dem Grundstück Britanniahütte 14-16 in 51469 Bergisch Gladbach. Mit dem 2024 erfolgten Kauf des Grundstücks Britanniahütte – mit zwei ehemaligen Industriehallen, die derzeit von der Feuerwehr Bergisch Gladbach genutzt werden – eröffnet sich die Möglichkeit, mehrere bislang über das gesamte Stadtgebiet verteilte Funktionen an einem Standort zu bündeln. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind Projektsteuerungsleistungen für dieses Vorhaben. Es wird wird ein Projektsteuerungsbüro gesucht, welches den Planungs- und Bauprozess für die Auftraggeberin entsprechend den Leistungsbildern der AHO – Leistungsphasen 2-5 – begleitet, die Beauftragung erfolgt stufenweise. Die Generalplanungsleistungen werden aktuell europaweit im Verhandlungsverfahren ausgeschrieben. Mit einem Zuschlag wird insoweit im 1. Quartal 2027 gerechnet. Mit der vorliegenden Ausschreibung wird ein Projektsteuerungsbüro gesucht, welches den Planungs- und Bauprozess für die Auftraggeberin entsprechend den Leistungsbildern der AHO – Leistungsphasen 2-5 – begleitet. Dabei erfolgt eine stufenweise Vergabe wie folgt: Stufe 1 = Leistungsphase 2 (Planung) Stufe 2 = Leistungsphase 3 (Ausführungsvorbereitung) Stufe 3 = Leistungsphase 4 (Ausführung) und 5 (Projektabschluss) Mit dem Zuschlag werden die Leistungen der Stufe 1 verbindlich beauftragt. Die Auftraggeberin hat das einseitige Recht, die Stufen 2 und 3 zusätzlich abzurufen; auf den Abruf besteht seitens des Auftragnehmers kein Anspruch. Sofern der Zuschlag in diesem Verfahren vor Zuschlagserteilung betreffend die Leistungen der Generalplanung erfolgt, behält sich die Auftraggeberin vor, den Auftragnehmer ergänzend auch unterstützend bei der Auswahl des Generalplaners beizuziehen, sodass auch Restleistungen der Leistungsphase 1 nach AHO eingebunden werden können. Einzelheiten ergeben sich aus den Vergabeunterlagen.

title: Germany – Construction work for school buildings – EPS | Erweiterung der Grund- und Mittelschule im Englischen Garten in Neuburg an der Donau – Planen und Bauen der drei Erweiterungsbauten in Modulbauweise (Totalunternehmer)
description: Die Stadt Neuburg an der Donau erweitert die Grund- und Mittelschule im Englischen Garten (Parkschulen) um drei Erweiterungsbauten in Modulbauweise. Die Erweiterungsbauten werden im sogenannten Rucksackprinzip unmittelbar vor die Westfassaden der Hochbauten 1 bis 3 gestellt und über Öffnungen in den Außenwänden an den Bestand angeschlossen.Die Erweiterungsbauten nehmen Klassen-, Differenzierungs- und Nebenräume auf. Toiletten und Treppenhäuser sind nicht enthalten, die Erschließung erfolgt über die Flure des Bestands. Das Raumprogramm ist einfach und wiederholt sich, es ist daher für eine serielle Fertigung im Werk geeignet.Parallel zur Erweiterung werden der Bestand saniert und brandschutztechnisch ertüchtigt. Diese Leistungen sind nicht Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens und werden getrennt vergeben. Alle Arbeiten finden im laufenden Schulbetrieb statt. Die Erweiterungsbauten müssen spätestens am 26.06.2028 nutzbar sein.Der Totalunternehmer übernimmt die Planung und Ausführung aller Leistungen der Erweiterungsbauten, die vom Modulsystem abhängen. Dies sind insbesondere:- Planung: Bieterentwurf, systemabhängige Ausführungsplanung, Werk- und Montageplanung, Tragwerksplanung sowie Brand- und Schallschutznachweise des Systems- Gründung: Spezialtiefbau (Mikrobohrpfähle), Erdarbeiten, Pfahlkopfbalken, Stahlbeton-Bodenplatte- Abbruch und Abfangung an den Westfassaden: Rückbau von Fenstern und Brüstungen, Herstellung der neuen Öffnungen, Stahlabfangungen, Schließen nicht mehr benötigter Öffnungen, Durchbrüche für die Haustechnik, Rückbau der Attika mit vorübergehender Dachentwässerung- Module: Fertigung im Werk, Transport und Montage- Gebäudehülle vor Ort: Fassadenbekleidung, Spenglerarbeiten, Retentionsdach mit Dämmung, Abdichtung, Entwässerung und Absturzsicherung- Innenausbau: Trockenbau (Trennwände, Vorsatzschalen, Akustikdecken), Estrich, Technikschrankwand und nachfolgende Oberflächen- Technische Gebäudeausrüstung in den Modulen: Heizung, Lüftung, Sanitär und Elektro bis zu den Übergabepunkten im Keller und im Elektroraum des Bestands- Anschluss an den Bestand: Anschlussfuge, Durchgänge, Rückbau der Abhangdecken in den Bestandsfluren, Staubschutzwände, Elektroleitungen an der Bestandsdecke bis zum ElektroraumNicht Gegenstand der Leistung sind die Sanierung und die Brandschutzertüchtigung des Bestands, die neuen Abhangdecken mit Deckenkoffer in den Bestandsfluren, die technische Gebäudeausrüstung ab den Übergabepunkten sowie die Außenanlagen. Die genaue Abgrenzung ergibt sich aus dem Leistungsprogramm und der Schnittstellenliste der Vergabeunterlagen der Stufe 2.Grundlage des Leistungsprogramms ist die Entwurfs- und Genehmigungsplanung des vom Auftraggeber beauftragten Objektplaners einschließlich der Leitdetails des Modulbaus. Die Bieter entwickeln diesen Entwurf für ihr System fort und erstellen die Ausführungs-, Werk- und Montageplanung (teilfunktionale Ausschreibung).Verbindlich vorgegeben sind Lage und Kubatur der drei Baukörper, das Raum- und Funktionsprogramm, die Geschosshöhen und Anschlusspunkte am Bestand, die bauphysikalischen und brandschutztechnischen Anforderungen sowie die gestalterischen Qualitäten nach Entwurfsplanung, Fassadenschnitten und Musterklassenzimmer. Konstruktionsaufbauten, Querschnitte, Systeme der Technischen Gebäudeausrüstung und Details der Entwurfsplanung sind Orientierungsvorgaben. Die Bieter können davon für ihr System abweichen, soweit die verbindlichen Vorgaben eingehalten werden.Die Erweiterungsbauten umfassen zusammen rund 2.400 m² Bruttogrundfläche. Sie haben jeweils drei Geschosse (Erdgeschoss bis 2. Obergeschoss) und schließen geschossgleich an die Hochbauten 1 bis 3 an. Die Entwurfsplanung sieht eine Holz-Stahl-Hybridbauweise mit hohem Vorfertigungsgrad und eine Gründung auf Mikrobohrpfählen vor. Die Ausschreibung ist systemoffen. Der Auftraggeber legt Wert auf einen hohen Anteil nachwachsender Baustoffe.An die Erweiterungsbauten werden die Anforderungen der Gebäudeklasse 5 gestellt. Brand- und Schallschutz der Wand- und Deckenaufbauten sind für das jeweilige System nachzuweisen.Die Schule liegt im Englischen Garten, einem Gartendenkmal im Landschaftsschutzgebiet. Teile des Parks gehören zum FFH- und Vogelschutzgebiet der Donauauen. Das Baufeld ist beengt. Grünflächen dürfen nur kurz und im unbedingt erforderlichen Umfang belegt werden.Die Arbeiten finden im laufenden Schulbetrieb statt. Die Öffnungen in den Westfassaden werden hinter Staubschutzwänden hergestellt und bis zur Montage vorübergehend verschlossen. Die Durchgänge werden erst nach dem Stellen der Module geöffnet. Die Rettungswege führen über die Bestandsflure und sind während der gesamten Bauzeit zu sichern, erforderlichenfalls über Maßnahmen des Interimsbrandschutzes.Der Vertrag wird als Totalunternehmervertrag unter Einbeziehung der VOB/B geschlossen. Die Vergütung erfolgt als Pauschalfestpreis. Der Vertragsentwurf ist Bestandteil der Vergabeunterlagen der Stufe 2. Die im Angebot zugesagten Termine, die Personalansätze und die Kennzahl der nachwachsenden Baustoffe werden Vertragsbestandteil.Der Beginn der Bauleistungen vor Ort ist ab dem 02.08.2027 vorgesehen. Nach dem Terminplan des Auftraggebers werden die Erweiterungsbauten nacheinander vor den Hochbauten 3, 1 und 2 errichtet und bis zum 07.04.2028, 17.05.2028 und 26.06.2028 fertiggestellt. Die Erweiterungsbauten müssen spätestens am 26.06.2028 an den Auftraggeber übergeben und nutzbar sein. Der Rahmenterminplan mit den verbindlichen Vertragsterminen ist Bestandteil der Vergabeunterlagen der Stufe 2.

title: Elektroarbeiten am Mitarbeitergebäude 2 - Fernmelde- und informationstechnische Anlagen
description: Erneuerung der Schwachstromanlagen, der Brandmelde- und Zutrittskontrollanlage sowie Erweiterung der einheitlich bestehenden Datennetzinfrastruktur – Mitarbeitergebäude 2, Universität Erfurt Im Rahmen der vollständigen Sanierung des Mitarbeitergebäudes 2 der Universität Erfurt werden die Schwachstromanlagen im Untergeschoss sowie in den vier oberen Etagen des Bürogebäudes umfassend erneuert und an die zukünftigen Nutzungsanforderungen angepasst. Die Maßnahme umfasst insbesondere die Erneuerung der Brandmeldeanlage, die Errichtung einer elektronischen Zutrittskontrollanlage sowie die Erweiterung und Anpassung der passiven und aktiven Datennetzinfrastruktur. Die bestehende Brandmeldeanlage wird vollständig erneuert. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst die Installation einer neuen Brandmeldezentrale sowie ca. 160 automatische Multisensormelder und ca. 130 akustische und optische Signalgeber. Ergänzend werden die erforderlichen Ein- und Ausgangsmodule, Steuer- und Überwachungseinrichtungen sowie Schnittstellen zur Ansteuerung und Überwachung weiterer gebäudetechnischer Anlagen installiert Weiterhin wird eine neue elektronische Zutrittskontrollanlage errichtet. Diese umfasst die erforderlichen Zutrittskontrollzentrale, Türsteuerungen, Kartenleser und sonstigen Systemkomponenten einschließlich der zugehörigen Verkabelung und Anbindung der Gebäudezugänge. Die Datennetzinfrastruktur wird umfangreich erneuert. Hierzu werden ca. 680 Datendosen einschließlich der vollständigen strukturierten Gebäudeverkabelung, Anschluss- und Verteilertechnik installiert. Die Anschlüsse dienen insbesondere der Versorgung der Büroarbeitsplätze sowie der Anbindung von WLAN-Access-Points zur flächendeckenden drahtlosen Netzwerkversorgung des Gebäudes. Zur Integration in die bestehende IT-Infrastruktur der Universität Erfurt ist das Gebäude über eine LWL-Verbindung mit den vorhandenen Bestandsnetzwerken der Liegenschaft zu verbinden. Hierzu gehören die erforderlichen LWL-Leitungen, Spleiß- und Patcharbeiten sowie die notwendigen passiven und aktiven Netzwerkkomponenten zur Herstellung der durchgängigen Netzwerkverbindung. Der Leistungsumfang beinhaltet sämtliche erforderlichen Installations-, Montage- und Anschlussarbeiten sowie die Inbetriebnahme, Funktionsprüfung und Dokumentation der neu errichteten Anlagen. Die Ausführung erfolgt unter Berücksichtigung der vorhandenen Bausubstanz und der betrieblichen Anforderungen des Bestandsgebäudes sowie in Abstimmung mit den parallel stattfindenden Sanierungs- und Ausbauarbeiten.

title: A borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock
description: A borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock Procurement of a borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock. The system shall include a wireline winch, a surface data acquisition unit, a three-arm caliper, a spinner flowmeter, a heat-pulse flowmeter, compatible accessories, and the necessary software. The equipment shall be suitable for measurements in deep, inclined, water-filled boreholes with nominal diameters of 56 mm and 76 mm, at operational depths of up to 1000 m measured along the borehole axis. All supplied components shall be mutually compatible and suitable for field operation. See the minimum requirements in the section Criteria for the object of procurement. Hankinnan kohteena on porareikien geofysikaalinen mittausjärjestelmä hydrogeologisiin tutkimuksiin rikkonaisessa kiteisessä kallioperässä. Järjestelmän tulee sisältää vaijerivinssi, pinnalla käytettävä tiedonkeruuyksikkö, kolmihaarainen kaliiperimittari, spinner-virtausmittari, lämpöpulssivirtausmittari, yhteensopivat lisävarusteet sekä tarvittavat ohjelmistot. Laitteiston tulee soveltua mittauksiin syvissä, kaltevissa ja vedellä täyttyneissä tutkimusrei’issä, joiden nimellishalkaisijat ovat 56 mm ja 76 mm. Laitteiston tulee mahdollistaa mittaukset 1000 metrin syvyyteen asti porareiän akselia pitkin mitattuna. Kaikkien toimitettavien komponenttien tulee olla keskenään yhteensopivia ja soveltua kenttäkäyttöön. Katso vähimmäisvaatimukset kohdasta hankinnan kohteen kriteerit.,

title: Germany – Administration, defence and social security services – [J4-25V-012] Neukonzeptionierung des "Handbuch der Ergonomie"
description: Das Handbuch der Ergonomie (HdE) ist eine umfangreiche Sammlung ergonomischen Fachwissens. Es dient dem Auftraggeber (AG) als zentrale mitgeltende Unterlage im Beschaffungsprozess und stellt eine unverzichtbare Säule für die Beantwortung ergonomischer Fragestellungen dar, mit dem Ziel, eine hohe Qualität in der Beschaffung und Entwicklung von Produkten zu gewährleisten. Gleichzeitig enthält es Daten und Angaben für Auftragnehmer (AN), wie Geräte/ Produkte ergonomisch konstruiert und ausgelegt werden. Ziel der im Rahmen des Vertrags zu erbringenden und im Folgenden näher beschriebenen Leistungen ist es, für die sowohl strukturelle als auch inhaltliche Gesamtüberarbeitung des HdE ein detailliertes Konzept zu erarbeiten, welches als Grundlage für die spätere Umsetzung dient: • Das Konzept soll basierend auf Bedarfsanalysen verschiedener Nutzergruppen neu ausgerichtet werden. Der Fokus soll hier auf einer Nutzbarkeit für die Bundeswehr und deren Bedürfnisse liegen. (Arbeitspaket 2) • Das HdE muss fachlich analysiert sowie auf seine Aktualität hin geprüft werden. (Arbeitspaket 3) • Erstellung von drei Konzepten, die das HdE zeitgemäß und übersichtlich aufbereiteten. Ein Konzeptvorschlag soll detailliert ausgearbeitet werden. (Arbeitspaket 4) • Neben der Erarbeitung des Konzeptes sollen alle notwendigen Vorarbeiten für die Gesamtüberarbeitung vorgenommen sowie geeignete Autoren für die Überarbeitung identifiziert werden. (Arbeitspaket 5)

title: Lunar Surface Logistics Architecture Study
description: The architecture study conducted as part of this SOW aims to inform and guide the strategic development of the targeted capability area identified in Section 4.1, necessary to enable a sustainable and resilient presence on the lunar surface. This study must support long-term exploration objectives below by identifying the functional, operational, and technical enablers required for successful human and robotic operations on the lunar surface, while also forward-looking beyond exploration of the Moon (e.g., Mars). The objectives of this LSEI Architecture Study are as follows: 1. Landscape Assessment and Strategic Outlook Provide a comprehensive scan of the domain’s current and emerging landscape within the targeted capability area. This includes reviewing applicable technologies, operational approaches, and development strategies, while identifying future needs and potential operating models. Where possible, conduct trade space analysis and evaluation between the various landscape items to determine advantages, disadvantages, and potential risks. The study must offer a clear scenario-based roadmap and outline key strategic pathways forward. 2. Sub-Architecture Specific sub-architecture for LSL must be defined and analyzed in detail. Sub-architecture must identify key system elements with their driving needs, interfaces, operational concepts, performance requirements and constraints, while also showing how it integrates into the broader lunar surface architecture. The objective is to ensure that sub-architectures are both individually robust and collectively interoperable, enabling modular evolution and alignment with the overall roadmap for lunar exploration and sustained operations. 3. Strategic Integration and Interoperability Clarify and map out strategic ties of the capability area to the integrated surface exploration architecture. The analysis must reflect technical feasibility and market interests while including considerations of interoperability, scalability, and alignment with long-term international exploration goals on the lunar surface. 4. Reference Framework for Development Establish a domain-specific reference architecture that informs future mission planning and guides concept definition, technology development, testing, and system-level integration. The reference architecture concept must support sustained human and robotic lunar surface exploration operations. The framework should support sustainable exploration practices and enduring surface operations. The architecture must demonstrate a clear evolution and progression over time from 2026 to 2040, showing how capabilities expand, integrate, and scale to support short-term missions through long-term sustainable lunar operations [RD-04]. This phased approach allows for the gradual expansion and adaptation of systems as technological capabilities and mission requirements mature. 5. Investment Guidance for Enabling Technologies Deliver recommendations for strategic technology investments that address capability gaps, reduce mission risks, and enhance outcomes in the lunar surface logistics sub-architecture. The proposed recommendations should also deliver terrestrial/societal benefits, with an emphasis on those that leverage existing or emerging national strengths. 6. Phased Implementation and Roadmap A key objective of the lunar architecture studies is to define phased implementation pathways that align with mission timelines and stakeholder priorities. The roadmap should illustrate how capabilities grow over time (from early demonstration missions to sustained lunar presence) highlighting critical milestones, decision points, and dependencies. It should also show how international, government, and commercial contributions can be integrated, ensuring interoperability and scalability while reducing technical and programmatic risk.

title: APN_Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3, CFB Borden ON
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3 CFB Borden, Ontario (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Borden, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN Number: 88280 Approximate Estimate: $168 million for both buildings Anticipated Posting Step 1: January 2027 Anticipated Posting Step 2: February 2027 Description: The project comprises the construction of two new five-storey training quarters buildings at CFB Borden, Ontario. The buildings will use a site-adapted design based on the existing Training Quarters Building S-166. The anticipated work includes building construction, mechanical and electrical systems, associated site development and connections to site services. The design will incorporate site-specific requirements and lessons learned from the existing building.  3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer or proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security screening requirement for each construction contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors or consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors or consultants that intend to submit a tender or a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers or proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors or consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors or consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor or consultant: Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI, have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase, meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer or proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Victor Shekofteh Contract Coordinator Defence Construction Canada 249-535-4651 victor.shekofteh@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer or proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. title: NPP - Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector
description: Trade Agreement: CFTA, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Colombia Free Trade agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement. Tendering Procedures: to all pre-qualified suppliers under the Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI under Crystallography Equipment. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Lowest cost Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: No Nature of Requirements: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT # E60PV-19EQUI ONLY, FOR THE PURCHASE OF LABORATORY AND SCIENTIFIC EQUIPMENT, PARTS AND ACCESSORIES, SERVICES AND SUPPLIES. Only Suppliers currently pre-qualified on Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI have been invited to bid. As a requirement of the Supply Arrangement, this notice is published on Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) for a period of 40 calendar days. The closing date published on this notice identifies how long the notice will be published. For the closing date of any solicitation under the supply arrangement, invited suppliers should refer to the solicitation documents. Suppliers that do not have a Supply Arrangement for the supply of Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies with Public Works and Government Services Canada, cannot submit a bid. Any bids received from suppliers not pre-qualified on the Supply Arrangement will not be evaluated. Suppliers may qualify under Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies, at any time. Interested suppliers should download solicitation document E60PV-19EQUI/D from CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba) and submit a response as per the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangement. Item : Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector Quantity: 1 The mandatory technical criteria are: # MANDATORY TECHNICAL CRITERIA M1 Must be capable of being installed on a TESCAN Mira3 XMH model scanning electron microscope M2 Must come equipped with a CMOS sensor, a phosphor screen, and fibre-optic coupling M3 Must be capable of collecting EBSD patterns with image sizes up to 1244x1024 M4 Must have pattern acquisition speeds of up to 5700 patterns per second at 156x128 resolution M5 Must allow analyses at beam currents as low as 400 pA and accelerating voltages as low as 5kV M6 Must be capable of angular resolution up to 0.05 degrees M7 Must have motorized screen elevation control and insertion/retraction control M8 Must come equipped with a 5 diode forescatter diode (FSD) array for orientation contrast, topographic contrast, and atomic number contrast imaging M9 Must come with a Windows PC workstation installed with software for data acquisition and processing. M10 Must be capable of simultaneous EDS/EBSD mapping with an X-Max 80 model EDS detector, permitting refined phase identification using sample chemistry. Note: The X-Max 80 is the exact model of EDS detector currently installed in the laboratory. We rely on a function where simultaneously collected EDS data is used to aid in the correct identification of crystallographically similar phases during automated EBSD analyses, and therefore any new EBSD detector must be compatible with our X-Max 80.

title: Radiologian erikoislääkärin etäpalvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat etänä tuotettavat radiologian erikoislääkärin palvelut Lapin hyvinvointialueelle. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen osa-alueeseen. Tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen joko yhteen tai kumpaankin osa-alueeseen. OSA-ALUE 1: Natiiviröntgenkuvien etälausuntopalvelu: Hankinnan kohteena on natiiviröntgenkuvien etälausuntopalvelut Lapin keskussairaalan, Länsi-Pohjan sairaalan ja Lapin hyvinvointialueen perusterveydenhuollon natiiviröntgentutkimuksista ja vertailu aiempiin kuva-arkistossa oleviin tutkimuksiin. OSA-ALUE 2: Radiologian etäpäivystyspalvelu Hankinnan kohteena on radiologian erikoislääkärin etäpäivystyspalvelu Lapin hyvinvointialueen tarpeeseen Lapin keskussairaalaan ja Länsi-Pohjan sairaalaan. Tarjouspyyntö muodostuu tästä hankintailmoituksesta liitteineen., Natiiviröntgenkuvien etälausuntopalvelu Natiiviröntgenkuvien etälausuntoja hankintaan hyvinvointialueelle keskimäärin arviolta noin 27000 kpl vuodessa, josta Lapin keskussairaalan ja perusterveydenhuollon osuus on keskimäärin noin 18 000 lausuntoa sekä Länsi-pohjan sairaalan osuus on keskimäärin noin 9000 lausuntoa. Arviot eivät muodosta tilaajille määräostovelvoitetta. Ostettavan palvelun määrä voivat vaihdella sopimuskaudella. Ostopalvelulla täydennetään hyvinvointialueen omaa palvelutuotantoa. Palvelua tuottavat radiologian erikoislääkärit on nimettävä tarjouslomakkeelle. Hankittavan palvelun sisältö on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus., Radiologian etäpäivystyspalvelu Päivystysaikaisella etäpäivystyspalvelulla tarkoitetaan ympärivuorokautista tai osavuorokautista päivystystä, joka toteutetaan etäyhteydellä. Tarjoaja sitoutuu tuottamaan palvelua vuoden kaikkina päivinä. * Arki-illan päivystyksen työvuorot ovat klo 15.00–08.00 (ma-to). * Perjantaipäivystys ja arkipyhää edeltävän päivän päivystystyövuoro on klo 15.00–08.00. * Viikonloppupäivystyksen työvuorot ovat (la ja su) ja arkipyhäpäivystyksen työvuoro on klo 08.00–08.00. Hankinnan kohteena olevan radiologin tehtäviin sisältyy • CT-lausunnot • MRI- lausunnot • Natiiviröntgenkuvalausunnot • Em. kuvauksiin liittyvät ohjeistukset • Muiden erikoisalojen lääkäreiden ja hoitohenkilökunnan päivystykselliset konsultaatiot Työvoiman tarve on arviolta 365 työvuoroa, sisältäen noin 4000-6000 CT-lausuntoa vuodessa, noin 150-300 MRI-lausuntoa vuodessa, noin 3000-4000 natiivikuvien lausuntoa vuodessa sekä em. muita työtehtäviä. Tarjoajan tulee tarjota vähintään viisi (5) ja enintään viisitoista (15) radiologian erikoislääkäriä täyttämään edellä kuvattu työvoiman tarve. Palvelua tuottavat radiologian erikoislääkärit on nimettävä tarjouslomakkeelle. Palveluntuottajalla on sopimuskaudella mahdollisuus vaihtaa tai lisätä palvelun tuottamiseen osallistuvia erikoislääkäreitä. Hankittavan palvelun sisältö on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus.,

title: Albania – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Preparation of audits, detailed design, tender documents, supervision of civil works for the implementation of energy efficiency measures in local public buildings across all four municipalities
description: This Contract covers the preparation of investment-ready documentation for 50 pre-selected local public buildings in the municipalities of Berat, Shkodër, Korçë and Përmet, including offices, kindergartens, libraries, and social and cultural centres. The Assignment includes the preparation of energy audits, detailed technical designs, building permit documentation, Bills of Quantities, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and PRAG-compliant tender documentation. All 50 buildings will be assessed and prioritised in accordance with DCM No. 468/2024 . Based on this prioritisation, buildings with a total gross floor area of at least 22,000 m² will be selected for the implementation of energy-efficiency measures under a subsequent Works Contract. The Contract also includes the supervision of the civil works implemented in the selected buildings. The Service Contract is structured in two phases, comprising a total of 60 months of service provision, with a 12-month interim period between the two phases. Phase 1, lasting 24 months, covers the energy audit, preparation of the detailed technical design and preparation of the tender dossier for the Works Contract. This phase will be followed by a 12-month interim period, during which the procurement procedure for the Works Contract is expected to take place and no services will be required under the Service Contract. Phase 2, lasting 36 months, will cover the supervision and monitoring of the Works, commencing upon the start of the Works Contract.

title: Table-Top Free Space Measuring System - USDA-ARS Auburn AL
description: This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of USDA ARS market research and does not itself constitute an RFQ. This requirement is covered under NAICS code 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources; Small Businesses; HUBZone small business; service-disabled, veteran-owned small business; 8(a) small business; veteran-owned small business; woman-owned small business; or small disadvantaged businesses; Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The USDA-ARS National Soil Dynamics laboratory (NSDL) is in need of a specialized microwave instrument which enables the user to measure reflection and transmission data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample. The following are the specification required for this instrument. 1. Small table-top frame for transmission and reflection measurements. 2. The frame with two probes at the proper alignment and distance for optimal measurements and has a versatile sample holder to allow for multiple specimen types and sizes. 3. The frame with two probes for a frequency range of at least 2.5 GHz to 20 GHz. 4. At least one pair of SMA cables designed for use up to at least 25 GHz. 5. Two probes should be able to be connected to a VNA. 6. Software for VNA that calculates the S-parameters. 7. Free Space Measurement Methods to characterize materials. 8. Enables the user to measure reflection and transmission of electromagnet waves data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample The Government does not intend to make an award based on responses to this inquiry. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Capability Statement All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Business concerns that possess the capabilities necessary to undertake this work should submit complete documentation of their capabilities to the Contracting Officer. Capability statements shall include the Contractors contact point to discuss their response. The capability statement should include: 1) Acknowledgement that they are able to provide the subject supplies/services being requested; 2) Interested vendors should identify their size standards in accordance with the Small Business Administration; 3) At least three previous requirements that are similar to the requirement include a discussion of the Contract type, delivery method, duration, etc.; 4) Any other information considered relevant to this requirement; and 5) The government requests that no proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in the response. Any vendor responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine their qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After review of the responses received, a combined synopsis/solicitation may be published on sam.gov depending on the responses received. All responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be received by the notice�s POC by the deadline in order to be considered. Responses may not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Inquiry. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Request.

title: Office of Hazardous Materials Safety Research Initiative � FY2026 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA)
description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.

title: Follow Up Request for Information for FDA Scientific Instrument Repair and Maintenance Recompete
description: Purpose and requested industry input The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requests completion of the attached Excel questionnaire to help the Government determine the best acquisition strategy and pricing structure for its scientific instrument repair and maintenance recompete. FDA seeks the most cost-effective approach with the least administrative burden while preserving responsive, qualified service. FDA intends to establish an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with firm-fixed-price (FFP) amounts or rates where practicable. Industry input will inform service delivery arrangements, whether service plans can be prepriced at IDIQ award and on what basis, service-manager handling charges, program management pricing, and platform capabilities. Written alternatives should explain their pricing basis, limitations, and expected benefit. Scope The anticipated scope includes managing, coordinating, and performing repair and maintenance of scientific instruments, integrated systems, and equipment supporting FDA laboratory operations at locations identified in task orders. Services include coverage administration, request intake and routing, quotations, preventive maintenance (PM) scheduling and tracking, diagnostics, repairs, parts, calibration when ordered, service records, reporting, and invoice reconciliation at the IDIQ and task-order levels. Representative equipment includes mass spectrometers; liquid and gas chromatographs; infrared, Raman, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometers; electron and optical microscopes; surface analysis instruments; DNA sequencers, analyzers, and extraction systems; microbial identification systems; flow cytometers; centrifuges; incubators and shakers; autoclaves; vacuum pumps; and laboratory refrigeration and freezers. Integrated systems may include multiple manufacturers� components, control computers, and software. These examples do not establish model-specific serviceability. For planning purposes, approximately 1,000 instruments are anticipated across FDA Centers in the United States and Puerto Rico. The preliminary site count includes approximately 25 laboratories within 17 cities: Dauphin Island, Alabama; Jefferson, Arkansas; Alameda and Irvine, California; Lakewood, Colorado; Atlanta, Georgia; Bedford Park, Illinois; Lenexa, Kansas; College Park, Laurel, and Silver Spring, Maryland; Winchester, Massachusetts; Detroit, Michigan; Jamaica, New York; Cincinnati, Ohio; Bothell, Washington; and San Juan, Puerto Rico. The questionnaire provides historical activity for informational and planning purposes only. These data have not been independently validated and do not constitute guaranteed demand or a verified count of future payable transactions. Coverage and pricing definitions Comprehensive plan and action. A purchased plan covers the technical services expressly identified for its coverage period, which may include PM, diagnostics, repairs, labor, parts, travel, and support, subject to stated exclusions. A comprehensive action is an authorized service request within that purchased coverage; included technical work is not separately charged again. As-needed action. An authorized request for technical service outside existing purchased coverage, including equipment without a plan or an excluded service. The provider price and required Government authorization are established before the work. As-needed describes demand and does not require time-and-materials pricing. Work included in repair-only or standalone PM plans remains covered work. Administration and service delivery definitions Service manager and service provider. The service manager administers coverage and coordinates requests. The service provider performs technical maintenance, repair, or calibration. Identify direct and subcontracted work. Provider price, handling charge, and PMO. The provider price pays for authorized technical work and included costs. A handling charge compensates request-level administration. Program management office (PMO) pricing addresses overall IDIQ and task-order administration, including scheduling, invoicing, PM tracking and management, and reporting. Industry should identify which activities each price includes. Work paid through one element must not be charged again through another; multiple quotes, visits, or invoices for the same request must not create duplicate handling charges. In-house and subcontracted repairs. In-house means work performed by the respondent�s own employees at FDA sites or its facilities. Subcontracted work is performed by another organization, including an original equipment manufacturer (OEM), authorized provider, or independent service firm. Identify applicable testing/calibration accreditation and scope separately from repair capability. Service priority and timing definitions Priority. Failure threatens time-sensitive work, research results, or sample integrity. The proposed on-site response target is within three business days; urgent support or faster response may be necessary. Standard. Failure affects operations, but a temporary workaround or alternate instrument permits work to continue. The proposed on-site response target is within seven business days. This corresponds to the questionnaire�s routine-response category. Non-time-critical. Service can be deferred without materially affecting current laboratory work, results, or samples. The proposed on-site response target is within twenty business days. This corresponds to the questionnaire�s non-critical category. FDA assigns priority based on operational impact. Performance Requirement: The contractor shall provide all management, tools, equipment, materials, labor, and supervision required to remove existing carpet and install new Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) flooring and vinyl base molding across approximately 2,887 sq. ft. on the 2nd Deck of the Multipurpose Building at USCG Station Cortez. 2. Active SAM Registration: Offerors must maintain an ACTIVE registration in SAM.gov at the time of proposal submission, prior to award, and throughout performance. NAICS Registration: Offerors should have NAICS code 238330 (Flooring Contractors) or related construction/renovation NAICS listed on their SAM profile. 4.4 Proposal Package Content Requirements To be deemed responsive, offerors must submit: Price Quote: A completed firm-fixed-price schedule breaking down labor, materials (LVP, adhesive, baseboards), subfloor preparation/grinding, and debris disposal. Technical Approach: Narrative demonstrating understanding of the Scope of Work (SOW), dust containment plan, installation methodology per manufacturer specifications, and estimated project schedule. Key Personnel Information: Identification of the Project Manager (PM) and designated alternate(s) including contact details and qualifications. Safety Plan: Written safety plan in compliance with FAR 52.236-13 and OSHA standards (29 CFR 1926). Areas covered include: Crew berthing spaces Administrative offices Communication Watchstander room Exclusions: This scope does not include upgrades to unrelated building systems, existing LPV spaces in sound condition, or bathroom flooring. 5.2 Material and Installation Specifications Flooring Material: Supply and install Lux Wood Cheyenne 7.25" x 48", 20 Mil Wear Layer / 5mm Core, with 1.55mm Pad LVP (approx. 2,887 sq. ft.). Baseboard: Supply and install 4-inch Coiled Vinyl Base throughout all finished areas. Subfloor Preparation: Complete mechanical grinding and adhesive removal on existing subfloors (allowance benchmark not to exceed $2.75/sq. ft.). Subfloor must be clean, level, dry, and inspected prior to installation. Adhesive: Utilize commercial adhesive strictly complying with the flooring manufacturer�s bonding specifications and DHS facility environmental guidelines. Debris & Containment: Install temporary dust and noise containment barriers to isolate adjacent active operational spaces. Contractor is responsible for removing all scrap, old carpet, adhesive residue, and packaging off-site daily. Clearance & Inspection: Ensure all interior doors swing freely with full functional clearance over new flooring transitions. 5.3 On-Site Conditions, Security & Personnel Requirements Key Personnel: The designated Project Manager must serve as the primary technical point of contact, be available by phone/email during duty hours (0800�1600 EST), and respond to technical requests within two (2) hours. Base Security & Badging: All workers must possess valid state-issued photo IDs, wear company-identifiable attire/badges at all times, and remain escorted in Government spaces as required. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large businesses will be used. This announcement is NOT a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the U.S. Government. Reese at shere.c.reese.civ@us.navy.mil by 2:00 pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 22 December 2025. Again, this is not a request for a proposal. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this RFI. Please note the information within this pre-solicitation synopsis will be updated and/or may change prior to an official synopsis/solicitation, if any. No phone calls will be accepted.

IT IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL BEING USED IN ACCORDANCE WITH FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) PART 10 TO IDENTIFY FIRMS POTENTIALLY CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE CAPABILITIES DESCRIBED HEREIN AND TO INFORM POTENTIAL FUTURE ACQUISITION PLANNING. THIS RFI IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, INVITATION FOR BID, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION, SOLICITATION, OR COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND CANNOT BE ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT TO FORM A BINDING CONTRACT. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR ISSUE A FUTURE SOLICITATION AS A RESULT OF THIS RFI. ANY QUANTITIES OR DELIVERY SCENARIOS REFERENCED IN THIS RFI ARE PROVIDED SOLELY TO SUPPORT MARKET RESEARCH AND CAPACITY PLANNING AND DO NOT CONSTITUTE A GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENT, ACQUISITION FORECAST, MINIMUM OR MAXIMUM PURCHASE QUANTITY, OR COMMITMENT TO PROCURE ANY QUANTITY. RESPONSE TO THIS RFI IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT REIMBURSE RESPONDENTS FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PREPARING OR SUBMITTING A RESPONSE, PROVIDING SUPPORTING INFORMATION, PARTICIPATING IN FOLLOW-UP DISCUSSIONS, OR PARTICIPATING IN ANY SUBSEQUENT MARKET RESEARCH ACTIVITY. INFORMATION SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI WILL NOT BE RETURNED. FAILURE TO RESPOND TO THIS RFI WILL NOT PRECLUDE A COMPANY FROM PARTICIPATING IN ANY FUTURE MARKET RESEARCH EFFORT, TECHNICAL DEMONSTRATION, OR COMPETITIVE ACQUISITION RELATED TO GROUP 1 AND GROUP 2 UAS TRAINING, MISSION PLANNING, MISSION REHEARSAL, SIMULATION, AND QUALIFICATION MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT OBLIGATED TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK OR COMMENTS REGARDING ANY RESPONSE. NO TELEPHONE RESPONSES WILL BE ACCEPTED. INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Respondents should address the capability areas and information requested in this RFI without assuming any relationship to that program�s requirements, acquisition approach, funding, schedule, or procurement quantities. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. These capabilities may enable operators to safely practice in realistic and challenging operational and threat environments, emergency procedures, and degraded system behaviors that may be impractical, unsafe, or cost-prohibitive to execute using live aircraft. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. The Government seeks to understand current industry capabilities, technology maturity, innovative approaches, best practices, and limitations relevant to these objectives. MARKET RESEARCH PROCESS This RFI represents the white-paper phase of Air PMO's market research effort. The Government may use information received to support capability development, requirements refinement, acquisition planning, evaluation of commercially available and emerging solutions, and potential procurement strategies. Following review of submitted white papers, the Government may invite selected respondents to participate in follow-up discussions or technical demonstrations to further assess the maturity, suitability, and applicability of proposed solutions. Selection for, or participation in, a follow-up activity does not constitute a competitive range determination, source-selection decision, commitment to procure, or preference for any future acquisition. Any invitation and associated instructions will be issued separately. The Government may elect not to conduct follow-up activities and is not obligated to provide feedback to respondents. INFORMATION REQUESTED Respondents should provide a concise white paper describing how their solution addresses the capability areas in this RFI. Responses should identify current capabilities separately from planned, developmental, or partner-provided capabilities. At a minimum, the white paper should address the following: Company profile, business size and socioeconomic status, Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and primary point(s) of contact. Executive summary of the proposed solution and the operational or training problem it addresses. Description of the complete solution, including software, hardware, peripherals, hosting or deployment model, licensing, and any Government-furnished equipment or services required. A capability cross-reference identifying each applicable Capability Area of Interest as currently available, configurable, developmental, not available, or provided by a third party. For developmental capabilities, identify the anticipated availability date and key dependencies. Supported Group 1 and Group 2 UAS platforms, flight models, ground control stations, hand controllers, payloads, mission-planning tools, and training environments, including the approach and estimated effort to add new aircraft or configurations. Technical maturity and commercial availability, including Technology Readiness Level or equivalent maturity evidence, operational use, customer base, relevant contracts, and available test or performance data. System architecture, interfaces, data formats, application programming interfaces, standards, modularity, and approach to integration with Government or third-party systems. Training-management, instructor, evaluation, after-action review, records-management, and qualification-management functionality. Cybersecurity, identity and access management, data protection, software-update, cloud or on-premises deployment, and authority-to-operate status or experience, as applicable. NDAA and supply-chain compliance status, including identification of any noncompliant components, planned remediation, dependencies, or assumptions. Implementation approach, schedule, lead times, training and support model, sustainment, warranties, upgrades, and product roadmap. title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: 6505--Sodium Bicarbonate (VA-27-00008836)
description: This Notice is a duplicate of the notice sent out 10/16/2026 for RFP 36E79726R0041 but with the updated RFP number due to the FY2027. PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Enterprise Procurement Office intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0005 for a restricted procurement for Sodium Bicarbonate Injection Vials, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD) (inclusive of Tricare Mail Order Pharmacies (TMOPs)), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA proposes to solicit for and award a firm-fixed requirements-type contract for sodium bicarbonate for injection (sodium bicarbonate) that is limited to suppliers with product manufactured in the United States in accordance with FAR 6.103-3 Industrial Mobilization: engineering, developmental, or research capability: or expert services. VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DOD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere on top of the successful offeror/contractor s label. Glass bottles ARE acceptable. All tablets/capsules/carton/bottles must be compatible with automated dispensing units (Baxter ATC Canisters, Opti-fill, etc.) Solicitation # 36E79727R0005 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 on or about November 23, 2026, with a tentative closing date of December 22, 2026. The NAICS code for this procurement is 325412. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at Sam.gov. No paper copies of the solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the solicitation will be accepted. Interested offerors are advised to continuously check Contracting Opportunities at SAM.gov for any changes to this solicitation. The National Stock Numbers (NSN) and Part Numbers (PN) are as follows: Item NSN PN ADAP 5985-99-958-0805 809632/000 The ADAP is a Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) on the KC-46. Each aircraft has two ADAPs installed. The KC-46 GPS ADAP is an advanced digital antenna that is able to receive GPS signals from multiple satellites simultaneously, allowing for more accurate and reliable navigation. This is particularly important for the KC-46, which is used for aerial refueling and transport missions and must be able to navigate accurately to rendezvous with other aircraft and deliver fuel or cargo. The service shall include providing obsolete parts resolution along with the necessary engineering to investigate Deficiency Reports and Material Improvement Projects (MIPs). The Government does not own the data or the rights to the data needed to compete the repair of this part. description: This announcement constitutes a Source Sought Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking interest from prospective offerors for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 award of the aforementioned project. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gauge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Construction and Dredging Communities, to include Small Businesses, as the Government must ensure there is adequate competition amongst the potential pool of responsible contractors. The notice is also soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for this large-scale construction project exceeding $35,000,000. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said notice or any follow-up information requested. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of an Invitation For Bid (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said sources sought notice or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The proposed project work will consist of nourishing approximately 4.1 miles shoreline along Kennedy Space Center between FDEP Range Monuments V-366 and V-386 in Brevard County, Florida. The project includes dredging approximately 2.5 million cubic yards (MCY) of material for construction of a beach berm and dune. Beach compatible sand for the project may be dredged from up to three (3) offshore borrow areas. Chester Shoals I is located east of Cape Canaveral in State waters and is centered approximately 1.7 miles offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Kennedy Shoals and Hetzel Shoals are located east of Cape Canaveral in Federal waters and are centered approximately 4.5 miles and 10 miles, respectively, offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Project work also includes, but is not limited to, beach tilling, turbidity monitoring, environmental species monitoring, and Munitions and Explosive of Concern (MEC) support. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 280 calendar days after issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including 60 calendar days to commence work. Magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The NAICS Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD SIZE IS $45,000,000.00. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about June 1, 2027 and the anticipated bid opening day is on or about July 1, 2027. title: TH-73 Aircraft Maintenance and Contractor Logistics Support (CLS)
description: 1. INTRODUCTION The Department of the Navy�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) (Aviation) - PMA-273 Naval Undergraduate Flight Training Systems and the Chief of Naval Air Training Command (CNATRA) require contractor services, supplies and tasks for the maintenance and logistics support of the United States Navy (USN) TH-73 aircraft program, also known as the Advanced Helicopter Training System (AHTS). This sources sought is being used as a market research tool pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Sources Sought will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this Sources Sought is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the request for proposal (RFP). The Government does not own a complete package of data or drawings for the TH-73 aircraft. The Government will make available any TH-73 data and drawings to which the Government has rights, and the Contractor cannot access. This is a follow-on requirement. The current contract information can be found in paragraph 3.0 below. The Government may hold a specific Industry Day for this requirement at a future date and time that has yet to be determined. More information will be released once additional details are known and able to be shared with Industry. References to CDRLs, CLINs, and Attachments are placeholders only. These documents are not and will not be provided with this Sources Sought Notice. The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: 1. Estimated Draft RFP Release: APRIL 2027 2. Estimated Final RFP Release: JULY 2027 3. Estimated Award Date: MAY 2028 4. Period of Performance/Ordering Period: 01-JUNE-2028 � 31-MAY-2035 Primary Work Location/Place of Performance: The anticipated primary place of performance is Naval Air Station Whiting Field (NASWF), Milton, FL. 2. DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The Government is anticipating this follow-on contract to be a single-award indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP), Fixed Hourly Rates and Cost Contract Line-Item Numbers (CLINs). The current contract information is as follows: Current Contractor: V2X AEROSPACE LLC Current Contract Number: N6134019D1010 - N6134021F0007 Current Contract Expiration Date: 31 May 2028 4. ELIGIBILITY The Government is considering North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 488190, Other Support Activities for Air Transportation, for this requirement. The corresponding small business size standard is $40.0 million in average annual receipts. The anticipated Product and Service Code (PSC) is J015, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment�Aircraft and Airframe Structural Components. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify its business size and applicable socioeconomic status, if any, in its capability statement. Note: For any resulting small business set-aside, the applicable limitations on subcontracting will be addressed in accordance with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (DEVIATION 2021-O0008, Revision 1) (FEB 2023). Respondents should review the full text at https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/policy/policyvault/USA000277-23-DPC.pdf To assist in our market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, if you are a small business interested in priming this effort and plan to utilize �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, please identify the name and CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) you intend to partner/subcontract with to meet the requirements as well as their size status under the NAICS that you as the prime would assign for their workshare. Information regarding any planned similarly situated entity should be included in answering any questions outlined in the Sources Sought Notice in order to assist the Government�s capability determination. 5. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested businesses shall submit a brief capabilities statement package demonstrating the ability to perform the services covered under the required capabilities, acceptable in either MS Word or PDF format. All responses shall include Sources Sought Notice name, Company Name, CAGE Code, Unique Entity Identifier (UIE) number, Company Address, Company website, Company Business Size and list of NAICS code(s) under which goods and services are provided, and Points of Contact (POC), including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Additionally, interested parties should address the following questions in their responses: What type of work has your company performed in the past within the last five years in support of the same or similar requirement? Has your company managed a task of this nature within the last five years? If so, please provide details. Has your company managed a team of subcontractors before? If so, provide details. Provide details on your intended management approach for meeting the requirements of a contract of this scope/complexity/magnitude. How will you staff this effort with qualified personnel? A description of your team with roles and responsibilities. All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this Sources Sought Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought Notice. No classified information shall be submitted in response to this Sources Sought. The capability statement package submissions must be received no later than 5:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on 22 December 2026. Submissions shall be electronically submitted via email to the Contract Specialist, Ms. Natasha Gompers at natasha.a.gompers.civ@us.navy.mil with copies to the Contracting Officer, Ms. Kathleen Dougherty at kathleen.c.dougherty.civ@us.navy.mil. description: Amendment 2: Changes the PPQ. - - - Solicitation Amendment -0001 answers Offeror questions. title: N16.14 MP-080191 - Upn.Tavannes-Bözingenfeld - APR GC phase MP jusqu'à la mise en service - Phases 32 à 53 (Auteur de projet avec DLT) (ID 12015)
description:
Le tronçon s’étend entre les Pk 69.250 et Pk 76.500, intégrant le tunnel de la Rochette, le tunnel de Pierre Pertuis, le tunnel de la Côte de Chaux, le tunnel Sous les Roches, la TC de la Métairie de Nidau et la TC de La Heutte.

Les objectifs généraux du mandat sont de poursuivre les études et la réalisation de l’entretien et de l'assainissement des installations de signalisation en lien avec l’UPlaNS N16 Tavannes – Bözingenfeld.

Les prestations du présent marché correspondent aux prestations (SIA MP, PP 32, 41, 51, 52, 53) d’auteur de projet (APR – Ingénieur GC) pour les secteurs TP4-TP5 à savoir le secteur Tavannes (y compris le tunnel de la Rochette) - La Heutte;

La réalisation des phases de prestations du mandat concerne notamment les éléments suivants :

·               Mise en œuvre des nouveaux portiques, potences (11 emplacements), barres-tunnels, consoles et mâts comprenant l’analyse et la proposition du type de support, l’optimisation du positionnement, en relation avec les normes de signalisation et les équipements existants, le dimensionnement des nouvelles structures porteuses et de leurs fondations, la vérification des impacts sur les ouvrages et aménagements existants (viaducs, talus, etc.), ainsi que les raccordements nécessaires ;

·               Analyse et vérification/dimensionnement des portiques et potences existants ;

·               Analyse et vérification/dimensionnement des éléments de retenue au droit des portiques et potences existants et nouveaux ;

·               Les aspects GC liés aux nouvelles infrastructures en lien avec le BSA, telles que fouilles pour tous les raccordements BSA et de signalisation, y compris nouvelles chambres éventuelles ;

·               Remplacement et /ou assainissement des couvercles de gatics existants, y compris renouvellement des cadres en béton, et compléments éventuels nécessaires selon réévaluation en phase MP ;

·               Gestion de la dépose et de la remise en place des dallettes de caniveaux, y compris mises en dépôt provisoire et remplacements nécessaires ;

·               Coordination de la signalisation et des marquages provisoires en phases chantier pour les travaux de GC en collaboration avec les autres mandataires ;

De réaliser les études pour les travaux GC nécessaire à l’APR BSA pour la réalisation de l’entretien et l'assainissement des installations BSA

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023
description: De toekomst van de ICT en bijbehorende dienstverlening voor onderwijs- en onderzoek ligt volgens SURF én de leden voor een belangrijk deel in de cloud. De leden (instellingen) willen daarom flexibel gebruik kunnen maken van de cloud en deze combineren met eigen ICT-infrastructuren (hybride infrastructuur). Overgang naar de cloud is in de praktijk geen eenvoudige stap, en voor veel instellingen geldt dat er weinig ervaring mee is opgedaan. Er kunnen daardoor onverwachte uitdagingen ontstaan tijdens de uitvoering van cloud projecten alsook in de beheerfase erna. De initieel beoogde voordelen worden dan niet behaald waardoor afbreukrisico c.q. kapitaalvernietiging kan ontstaan. Om instellingen te ondersteunen bij deze uitdagingen is het dan ook gewenst om SURFcumulus Professional Services via een SURF aanbesteding voor hen beschikbaar te maken. SURF kiest ervoor om dit via een DAS te laten verlopen. De levering van SURFcumulus Professional Services is nadrukkelijk gekoppeld aan de SURFcumulus dienst. Concreet gaat het om uitvoerende, gangbare dienstverlening bedoeld voor cloud implementatie, -migratie en -beheer. Levering gebeurt op basis van vaste prijs en vaste opleverdatum. Een nadere omschrijving van de dienstverleningonderdelen is als volgt: Inrichten van een cloud landing zone, geïntegreerd in de bestaande (hybride) architectuur van een instelling, ten minste omvattend: Account setup: gebaseerd op de administratieve organsiatie, compliance richtlijnen, bestaande omgevingen en structuren van de instelling. Network configuratie: volgens richtlijnen, binnen cloud omgevingen en tussen on-premise en deze cloud omgevingen. Security baseline: identity en access management op basis van SURFconext, bechikbaarheid van gestandaardiseerde, hardened machine images, security policies, network monitoring en log analytics. Automation: gestandaardiseerde inrichting van security, governance, and kostenoptimalisatie. Uitvoeren/ondersteunen van cloud migraties, door middel van: Lift-and-shift migratie scenario: het zonder ingrijpende wijzigingen (deels) verplaatsen van een ICT infrastructuur uit een datacenter naar de cloud. Re-design migratie scenario: het cloud ready maken van (een deel van) een bestaande ICT infrastructuur en/of het implementeren van vervangende, nieuw te bouwen oplossingen waardoor het potentieel van de cloud optimaal benut kan worden. Leveren van cloud managed services in de (hybride) cloud infrastructuur, waaronder bijv.: Operations (accountbeheer, software update management, licentiebeheer, netwerkbeheer, backup & restore, monitoring, platformbeheer) Application management (technisch applicatiebeheer, functioneel applicatiebeheer, gegevensbeheer, applicatie configuratiebeheer) Service support (incident-, problem- & change management, multi vendor coordinatie, tweede en derdelijns support, escalatie afhandeling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity-, cost- en continuity management) Informatie beveiliging en privacy bescherming (detectie, preventie, rapportage, bijsturing). Zie verder het toegevoegde document "Toelatingsleidraad DAS SURFcumulus Professional Services".
